title: Signed at or after the key's revocation: the model rejects, V1 does not evaluate revocation
scenario: The trace is a forgery: bytes signed at the revocation instant (signed = revoked = anchor) by a key that is then still usable. P6's correct model rejects it. V1 does not evaluate revocation (A9 cases e, e'): such bytes are byte-for-byte an ordinary valid bundle, VALID_STRICT with revocation NOT_EVALUATED, and nothing in the bundle distinguishes them from case e's honest bytes. A-e's bundle therefore realises the vector; the relying party must not read non-revocation into it.
base: honest bundle (A-a); revocation happens out of band

mutations.detail: bytes unchanged; the slot-B key is revoked out of band

choices: Model/V1 divergence, stated: the model's P6 prediction (reject) is NOT the V1 expectation. The vector follows V1: VALID_STRICT with revocation NOT_EVALUATED (A9.4; A9 cases e, e'). Listed so the divergence is visible, not as a test of P6.

needs: A real receipt; no revocation channel is consulted.

subcases.construction: A-a bytes unchanged; the slot-B key is revoked out of band (nothing in the bundle or trust configuration changes)

analogous: A-e2 (revoked before declared; same bytes, different out-of-band timing)

subcases.T_derivation: T = nTime(h*) of the fixture's own receipt proof and headers (a_sig and receipt_anchor as stamped; rows 11.1-11.4 pass); U = 7200 + max nTime(h*..h*+5) (A10.1.1)

analogous_to: A-e2 (revoked before declared; same bytes, different out-of-band timing)
